Thinking out loud just for the LOLs

A note on what I care about on my spare time

I've just got back from Asia from a brutal work trip. For two months I had to endure things that fell apart, put them back together, and make sure they continuously run without me being there. I work in a startup. I love working there. I am now pretty much a senior engineer and have grown to be a highly versatile engineer. However, seemingly my two month speed run dealt a toll on me, and I needed a break. Not a vacation, a break.

I came back to Boston at the first week of November and decided to take a long break. As I was relaxing on a coffee shop around MIT campus, I stumbled on this podcast saying things like someone getting the job they didn't think to have. One thing that struck me was that thinking out loud in public shows that there are things you care about in your free time. There is some truth of that.

I think as individuals living in a complex system which is this world, there are so many things that are out of our control and so little that are within our control. Everything is just about turning the knobs of what little we have to control, which is what counts. Imagine yourself being transported to 2000 years ago and the only thing you can bring with you is knowledge from the 21st century - what can you do? There isn’t much you can do other than leveraging what little you have in that time. The one most important 21st century knowledge is probably just sanitation - the fact that you know how disease spread and how to clean yourself - is probably a skill that can get you employed by the chief of a village you ran into. That or you get hanged for being a witch. But even so, people 2000 years ago aren’t that stupid. If anything, their intelligence is equal to humans today. The only difference here is we are standing on the knowledge and infrastructure build by thousands of brilliant humans before us. Today, I have an all knowing deity that I can ask anytime and anywhere about anything whenever I want for $20 a month (i.e. Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, etc.). Back then people are either trial and erroring things at the cost of their lives or basically just moving stones as a career their entire life to build the pyramid.

I guess the point I’m trying to say is that the only thing we can do as individuals in any part of society in this blue pale dot is probably only one thing: build. Making things is what we are born to do - Re: opposable thumbs and big ass brains. What are we making and towards what? Solving world hunger? Raising a family? Helping your neighbors? Making lives easier? Easier how? Until what point? My answer is - who cares? I build stuff because that’s what gives me purpose and fulfillment. I don’t know why, but it is the way it is. Not only does it give this sense of fulfillment to my monkey brain, but it is also a way to survive - I create service and goods in exchange of value, i.e. money. But it doesn’t have to be like that all the time. Sometimes we just do things for the LOLs, also known as just for fun because it’s like entertainment and to fill our curiosity. It doesn’t matter what is the end goal - just do it. If, in the end, it ends up having the human race creating a super powerful being that transcends digital and analog world, like an AGI that manifest itself to flesh and deemed us biological beings obsolete and kills us all, so be it. Life is short anyway. Sometimes, the best way to go about is to just go with your instincts where some guardrails are in place, and then constantly iterate. We are beings that iterate. Until then, I want to keep building stuff because I’m curious and have some adult money to play around with.

Honestly, that’s as far as thinking out loud as it gets for me in this past 20 minutes. I will definitely have more. Maybe in the form of nuts and bolts or melted plastic with electric circuits.
